architectureNotes:
opencommit is a single-process CLI, roughly: cli.ts (cleye) → commands/{commit,config,githook,commitlint,setup,models} → generateCommitMessageFromGitDiff.ts (budgeting + chunking) → prompts.ts (prompt assembly) → utils/engine.ts (provider switch) → engine/*.ts. Config is read once at module load via a top-level `const config = getConfig()` in several files (prompts.ts, commit.ts, commitlint/prompts.ts) — a notable coupling that makes those modules non-reentrant and is exactly why `handleModelNotFoundError` has to write global config and recurse to change a model mid-run. Any vendored module must have that module-level `getConfig()` dependency injected as a parameter instead.

Two prompt paths diverge at `getMainCommitPrompt()`: the default conventional-commit path, and the `@commitlint` path which substitutes both the system prompt (rules inferred from the repo's commitlint config) and the few-shot assistant example (LLM-generated once, hash-cached in `.opencommit-commitlint`). Both paths always send exactly three seed messages plus the diff as a fourth user message.

aio-ade's equivalent stack is materially more sophisticated on the execution side and materially thinner on the prompt side. Execution: src/shared/commit-message-agent-spec.ts is a registry of CLI agents (claude, codex, opencode, pi, amp, cursor) with per-agent buildArgs, promptDelivery (argv vs stdin), static-or-dynamic model sources and stdout parsers for model discovery; src/main/text-generation/commit-message-text-generation.ts handles local spawn, WSL-aware spawn, Windows batch-argument safety, SSH remote execution, a 60 s timeout, a 4 MB output cap, cancellation, path redaction of failure output, and a macOS Tailscale DNS hint. src/shared/source-control-ai*.ts adds per-operation action recipes, template variables, and per-repo/per-host overrides. None of that exists in opencommit. Conversely aio-ade's actual prompt is ~40 lines of hardcoded English rules in src/shared/commit-message-generation.ts (plus a near-duplicate base prompt in src/shared/commit-message-prompt.ts — worth noting these two have drifted and both are live).

So the integration shape is clear: keep aio-ade's execution layer untouched and replace/extend only the prompt-construction layer (`buildCommitMessagePrompt`) and the diff-collection layer (`getStagedCommitContext`).

features.howItWorks: `src/modules/commitlint/pwd-commitlint.ts` resolves `@commitlint/load` out of the repo's own node_modules (handles both CJS <=v18 and ESM >=v19, plus pnpm layouts via a searchPaths loop) and calls `load()` to get a `QualifiedConfig`. `src/modules/commitlint/prompts.ts` holds a `rulesPrompts` table mapping ~35 rule names (`type-enum`, `subject-max-length`, `header-case`, `body-leading-blank`, `scope-empty`, `signed-off-by`, …) onto generator functions built from 8 primitives in `llmReadableRules` (caseRule/emptyRule/enumRule/enumTypeRule/fullStopRule/maxLengthRule/minLengthRule/blankline). `inferPromptsFromCommitlintConfig()` skips `RuleConfigSeverity.Disabled` rules and emits e.g. "The subject should never have 72 characters or more." `type-enum` additionally mines `config.prompt.questions.type.enum[t].description` for per-type descriptions. Unknown (plugin) rules degrade to a visible "Please manually set the prompt for rule X" placeholder rather than being dropped. The whole commitlint config is sha256-hashed (`crypto.ts`) and cached to `.opencommit-commitlint` in the repo root; `configureCommitlintIntegration()` regenerates only when the hash changes or `oco commitlint force` is run.
features.name: Commitlint config → LLM-readable rules (the standout feature)
features.valueForAioIde: aio-ade has ZERO commitlint awareness — `grep -rn commitlint src/` in D:\Project\.15_Ai0-IDE returns nothing. Its prompt hardcodes English "imperative mood, <= 72 chars" rules in src/shared/commit-message-generation.ts, so on any repo with a commitlint hook the generated message can be rejected by the very commit it is about to run. aio-ade already surfaces `fixCommitFailure` as a source-control action, meaning it currently pays for this with a round-trip agent fix instead of getting it right first time. The rule→prose table is pure, dependency-light, and testable — the single highest-value port here.
features.whatItDoes: Loads the target repo's own @commitlint configuration at runtime and mechanically translates every rule into a natural-language instruction, then constrains the model with that rule list so generated messages actually pass `commitlint`.

features.howItWorks: `src/prompts.ts` composes `INIT_MAIN_PROMPT` out of small getters: `getCommitConvention(fullGitMojiSpec)` returns FULL_GITMOJI_SPEC (~70 emoji/description pairs), GITMOJI_HELP (10 pairs) or CONVENTIONAL_COMMIT_KEYWORDS ('fix, feat, build, chore, ci, docs, style, refactor, perf, test'); `getDescriptionInstruction()` from OCO_DESCRIPTION; `getOneLineCommitInstruction()` from OCO_ONE_LINE_COMMIT; `getScopeInstruction()` from OCO_OMIT_SCOPE emitting 'Use the format: <type>: <subject>'. The two gitmoji tiers exist explicitly to control token cost. Keys are declared in `CONFIG_KEYS` in src/commands/config.ts with per-key validators and a `oco config describe` self-documenting command.
features.name: Structured commit-convention toggles instead of one free-text prompt box
features.valueForAioIde: aio-ade's only style control is `sourceControlAi.instructionsByOperation` (free text) plus `commitMessageAi.customPrompt` — see src/shared/source-control-ai-types.ts. Every user has to hand-write "Use Conventional Commits" (which is literally the string used across aio-ade's own test fixtures). Discrete toggles are cheap UI in the existing CommitMessageAiPane.tsx, produce consistent prompts, and are the difference between a feature people configure once and a text box they leave empty.
features.whatItDoes: Exposes commit style as discrete, composable config flags — conventional-commit keywords, gitmoji on/off, full-vs-10-emoji gitmoji spec, omit scope, one-line only, add WHY description — and assembles the system prompt from them.

features.howItWorks: `getMainCommitPrompt()` in src/prompts.ts returns `[INIT_MAIN_PROMPT, INIT_DIFF_PROMPT, INIT_CONSISTENCY_PROMPT(translation)]`. The assistant example is not hardcoded English — it is pulled per-locale from `src/i18n/<locale>.json` (`commitFix`, `commitFeat`, `commitFixOmitScope`, `commitFeatOmitScope`, `commitDescription`) and assembled by `getConsistencyContent()`, which honors OCO_EMOJI (prefixing 🐛/✨ and stripping the redundant `fix(...)`/`feat(...)` word via `removeConventionalCommitWord`), OCO_ONE_LINE_COMMIT (drops the second example) and OCO_OMIT_SCOPE (swaps to the scope-less variants). For the commitlint path the assistant example is *generated once by the LLM itself* from the inferred rules and cached in `.opencommit-commitlint`.
features.name: Few-shot consistency prompt (example diff + example answer)
features.valueForAioIde: aio-ade's prompt (src/shared/commit-message-generation.ts buildCommitMessagePrompt) is strictly zero-shot prose rules. One worked example is the cheapest known way to lock output shape and kill preamble/fence drift — aio-ade currently compensates after the fact with a fairly elaborate cleanup pass (cleanGeneratedCommitMessage in src/shared/commit-message-agent-output.ts strips fences, 'Generating…' lines, list markers). Cheaper to prevent than to scrub.
features.whatItDoes: Every request carries a canned 3-message conversation: system rules, a fixed realistic `git diff` (INIT_DIFF_PROMPT, a port→PORT rename plus process.env.PORT), and an assistant turn showing the exact expected output shape for that diff.

features.howItWorks: `isFileExcludedFromDiff()` in src/utils/git.ts filters on `.lock`, `-lock.`, `.svg`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.webp`, `.gif`; `getDiff({files})` then runs `git diff --staged -- <diffableFiles>` and prints an outro naming the excluded ones. Independently, `getOpenCommitIgnore()` reads a repo-root `.opencommitignore` through the `ignore` package and applies it in `getStagedFiles()`, so users can add e.g. `**/*.jpg` or generated dirs.
features.name: Exclude lockfiles and binaries from the staged diff
features.valueForAioIde: Confirmed gap. `getStagedCommitContext()` in src/main/git/status.ts runs `git diff --cached --patch --minimal --no-color --no-ext-diff` with no pathspec exclusions at all; grep for lockfile/exclude filtering in that file finds nothing. So a `pnpm-lock.yaml` bump silently eats a large share of aio-ade's 200 KB STAGED_DIFF_BYTE_BUDGET (and its fair-share allocator will dutifully hand the lockfile an equal slice, starving the real code). This is a ~15-line fix with an outsized quality effect on a pnpm monorepo.
features.whatItDoes: Drops files that produce huge, semantically worthless diffs before git is even asked for the patch, and tells the user which files were skipped.

features.howItWorks: `OCO_LANGUAGE` accepts a locale code or a human alias — `I18N_CONFIG_ALIAS` in src/i18n/index.ts maps 'de'|'German'|'Deutsch' → de, 'vi_VN'|'Vietnamese'|'tiếng Việt' → vi_VN, etc., resolved by `getI18nLocal()`. The resolved locale supplies two things: the literal string injected into the prompt (`Use ${language} for the commit message.`, where language is `translation.localLanguage`, e.g. "vietnamese") and the localized few-shot assistant example from src/i18n/<locale>.json. 19 locales shipped: en, zh_CN, zh_TW, ja, ko, cs, de, fr, it, nl, pt_br, vi_VN, es_ES, sv, ru, id_ID, pl, tr, th.
features.name: Commit-message output language (i18n of the message itself, not the UI)
features.valueForAioIde: No equivalent — grep for language/locale in aio-ade's commit-message path returns nothing, and the base prompt is English-only. Given aio-ade's authors and the Vietnamese-language context in this workspace, a language selector plus a localized example is directly relevant. The pairing matters: a bare "answer in Vietnamese" instruction without a localized example tends to also translate the `feat:` keyword, which breaks conventional-commit linting. opencommit's vi_VN.json shows the correct shape.
features.whatItDoes: Generates the commit message in any of 19 languages while keeping the conventional-commit type keywords in English.

features.howItWorks: `src/utils/removeContentTags.ts` walks the string tracking open/close depth rather than regexing, so nested `<think>` survives; it then collapses runs of spaces/tabs (preserving newlines) and trims. Wired into engines that talk to reasoning models — notably the ollama engine with the `ollamaThink` config flag on `AiEngineConfig`.
features.name: Strip <think> reasoning blocks from model output
features.valueForAioIde: aio-ade's `cleanGeneratedCommitMessage` (src/shared/commit-message-agent-output.ts) strips code fences, `Generating…`/`Thinking…` first lines, and leading list markers — but has no tag-based stripping. Since aio-ade deliberately drives reasoning-capable CLIs (its commit-message agent spec exposes thinking levels up to 'max' for Claude and 'xhigh' for Codex, per src/shared/commit-message-agent-spec.ts), a CLI that emits a reasoning block inline lands verbatim in the commit box. ~60 lines, no deps, drops straight into the existing cleanup pipeline.
features.whatItDoes: Removes `<think>…</think>` (or any named tag) regions from the raw response before it is treated as a commit message, with correct handling of nested tags.

features.howItWorks: `tokenCount()` in src/utils/tokenCount.ts encodes with `@dqbd/tiktoken` cl100k_base and frees the encoder each call. In generateCommitMessageFromGitDiff.ts: `MAX_REQUEST_TOKENS = OCO_TOKENS_MAX_INPUT - ADJUSTMENT_FACTOR(20) - INIT_MESSAGES_PROMPT_LENGTH - OCO_TOKENS_MAX_OUTPUT`, where the prompt length is summed per message with `+4` tokens of per-message chat overhead.
features.name: Token-accurate budgeting instead of byte budgeting
features.valueForAioIde: aio-ade budgets in bytes (STAGED_DIFF_BYTE_BUDGET = 200_000 in src/shared/commit-message-prompt.ts). For CLI-agent invocation that is arguably the *right* call — aio-ade never sees a token limit, it pipes to `claude -p`/`codex`, and shipping cl100k_base BPE ranks into an Electron bundle costs real megabytes while being wrong for Claude and Codex tokenizers anyway. Worth understanding, not worth adopting.
features.whatItDoes: Sizes the diff against the model's real context window using a BPE tokenizer, reserving room for the system prompt and the reserved output tokens.

features.howItWorks: `getCommitMsgsPromisesFromFileDiffs()` splits on `diff --git `, then `mergeDiffs()` (src/utils/mergeDiffs.ts) greedily concatenates adjacent file diffs while they fit. Any single file still over budget goes to `getMessagesPromisesByChangesInFile()`, which splits on the `@@ ` hunk header, re-merges hunks, re-prepends the file header to each chunk, and falls back to `splitDiff()` (line-boundary, with hard character slicing for pathological single lines). All resulting prompts run through `Promise.all` and the messages are joined with `\n\n`.
features.name: Per-file diff chunking with parallel LLM calls and message merge
features.valueForAioIde: aio-ade truncates instead: `truncateDiffForPrompt` water-fills the byte budget fairly across file sections and clips on line boundaries (src/shared/commit-message-prompt.ts). aio-ade's approach is honestly better for message quality — opencommit's join produces N stapled-together commit messages for one commit, which reads badly. The genuinely portable idea is the *hunk-aware* split: aio-ade clips a file mid-file, whereas splitting on `@@ ` and re-prepending the file header keeps every surviving chunk a valid, self-describing diff. Worth folding into truncateDiffForPrompt; the parallel-call/merge architecture is not.
features.whatItDoes: When the diff exceeds the budget, splits it into per-file then per-hunk pieces, packs pieces greedily to fill the budget, generates a commit message per piece in parallel, and concatenates the results.

features.howItWorks: `src/commands/githook.ts`: resolves the hook dir via `git config core.hooksPath` (falling back to `.git/hooks`), then `fs.symlink(__filename, <hooksPath>/prepare-commit-msg, 'file')` + `chmod 0o755`. It refuses to clobber a pre-existing different hook, and on `unset` verifies `fs.realpath` matches its own path before removing. Reentrancy: `isHookCalled()` checks whether `process.argv[1]` ends with the hook path, and cli.ts branches to `prepareCommitMessageHook()` before any other command. The hook handler (src/commands/prepare-commit-msg-hook.ts) reads argv `[messageFilePath, commitSource]`, returns immediately if `commitSource` is set (so merge/squash/`-m` commits are untouched), and writes the message *commented out* with a '# Remove the # above to use this generated commit message.' banner unless `OCO_HOOK_AUTO_UNCOMMENT=true`. On failure it writes the error into the message file as `#`-prefixed lines instead of blocking the commit.
features.name: prepare-commit-msg git hook install/uninstall
features.valueForAioIde: aio-ade has no git-hook installation for commit messages (grep: nothing). Its AI commit message only exists inside the app's Source Control panel. aio-ade's whole premise is worktrees driven by external CLI agents, where commits frequently happen in a terminal pane or by the agent itself — those paths get no AI message today. Two details are worth stealing verbatim regardless of whether you ship the hook: the `commitSource`-set early return, and the commented-out-by-default write (fail-safe: a hook bug can never silently commit an LLM message).
features.whatItDoes: Registers the tool as git's `prepare-commit-msg` hook so commits made from any client (bare `git commit`, VS Code, JetBrains, lazygit) get an AI-drafted message pre-filled in the editor.

features.howItWorks: `checkMessageTemplate()` in src/commands/commit.ts scans extra argv for a token containing `config.OCO_MESSAGE_TEMPLATE_PLACEHOLDER` (default `$msg`), removes that token from the args forwarded to `git commit`, and does `messageTemplate.replace(placeholder, commitMessage)`.
features.name: Message template placeholder ($msg)
features.valueForAioIde: Mostly already covered and arguably better: aio-ade's `SOURCE_CONTROL_ACTION_VARIABLES` (src/shared/source-control-ai-action-variables.ts) gives commitMessage the `{basePrompt}`, `{branch}`, `{stagedFiles}`, `{stagedPatch}`, `{linkedIssue}` variables, with `formatLinkedIssueTemplateValue` handling the unlinked case. The one thing missing is post-generation wrapping — aio-ade templates the *prompt*, not the *result*, so it must ask the model to include `Fixes #123` and hope. A deterministic post-format template would be strictly more reliable.
features.whatItDoes: Lets the user wrap the generated message in a template supplied on the command line, e.g. `oco '#205: $msg'`, for issue/ticket prefixes.

features.howItWorks: src/commands/config.ts (~1370 lines): `getEnvConfig()` dotenv-loads `<cwd>/.env` and JSON.parses scalars via `parseConfigVarValue`; `getGlobalConfig()` ini-parses `~/.opencommit`, seeding it from `DEFAULT_CONFIG` when absent; `getConfig()` merges env over global over defaults. Each `CONFIG_KEYS` entry has a validator (enum membership for OCO_AI_PROVIDER / OCO_PROMPT_MODULE, numeric bounds for token limits, `getI18nLocal` for OCO_LANGUAGE). `oco config describe [KEY]` prints the key's meaning, accepted values and default. Schema drift is handled by numbered migrations in src/migrations/ (`00_use_single_api_key_and_url`, `01_remove_obsolete_config_keys_from_global_file`, `02_set_missing_default_values`) run from cli.ts on every invocation.
features.name: Layered config: repo .env → global ~/.opencommit ini → defaults, with per-key validation and self-documentation
features.valueForAioIde: aio-ade already has an equivalent and richer layering — global `sourceControlAi` settings, per-repo `RepoSourceControlAiOverrides`, per-operation model overrides, and per-host model/discovery caches (src/shared/source-control-ai-types.ts, resolved by resolveSourceControlAiForOperation). The only transferable idea is a *repo-committed, checked-in* config file so a team shares one commit-message convention; aio-ade's repo overrides live in the user's own profile, not in the repo. Low priority.
features.whatItDoes: Merges configuration from three sources with repo-local winning, validates every value on write, and can describe every key and its accepted values from the CLI.

features.howItWorks: `isModelNotFoundError()` / `getSuggestedModels(provider, currentModel)` in src/utils/errors.ts against the per-provider `MODEL_LIST` and `RECOMMENDED_MODELS` maps; `handleModelNotFoundError()` in generateCommitMessageFromGitDiff.ts renders a `@clack/prompts` select (plus 'Enter custom model…'), writes via `setGlobalConfig` if confirmed, and recurses into `generateCommitMessageByDiff(..., retryWithModel)`. Sibling: `formatUserFriendlyError` + `PROVIDER_BILLING_URLS` turn quota errors into a link to the right billing page.
features.name: Model-not-found interactive recovery
features.valueForAioIde: aio-ade persists `discoveredModelsByAgent` / `discoveredModelsByAgentByHost` (src/shared/types.ts), so a stale selection after a CLI upgrade is a live failure mode — and today it surfaces as a raw CLI stderr excerpt. Recovering into 'model X is gone, pick from the models this CLI now reports' would use data aio-ade already stores. The concept ports; the code does not (opencommit maps API providers, aio-ade maps CLI agents).
features.whatItDoes: When a provider rejects the configured model, offers a picker of valid alternatives (flagging the recommended one), optionally saves the choice as default, and retries the same generation.

features.howItWorks: `src/engine/Engine.ts` declares `AiEngine { config: AiEngineConfig; client: Client; generateCommitMessage(messages: ChatCompletionMessageParam[]): Promise<string|null|undefined> }` with `AiEngineConfig { apiKey, model, maxTokensOutput, maxTokensInput, baseURL?, proxy?, customHeaders?, ollamaThink? }`. `src/utils/engine.ts` is a switch over `OCO_AI_PROVIDER_ENUM` → concrete engine. Providers: openai (default), anthropic, azure, gemini, mistral, ollama, llamacpp, mlx, flowise, groq (extends OpenAiEngine with Groq's baseURL), deepseek, aimlapi, openrouter, plus a `test` engine (src/engine/testAi.ts, TEST_MOCK_TYPES) used by the e2e suite. Cross-cutting concerns are separate utils: `proxy.ts` (OCO_PROXY, falling back to HTTPS_PROXY/HTTP_PROXY, `null` to disable), `customHeaders.ts` (JSON string → header map), `modelCache.ts` (per-provider model lists fetched from each provider's /models endpoint, cached in ~/.opencommit-models.json with a 7-day TTL and graceful fallback to hardcoded MODEL_LIST).
features.name: Provider abstraction (14 providers behind one interface)
features.valueForAioIde: Architecturally irrelevant and should be actively avoided. aio-ade deliberately has no API keys and no HTTP LLM calls — it spawns the user's already-authenticated CLI agents (`claude`, `codex`) as subprocesses; see src/shared/commit-message-agent-spec.ts (promptDelivery 'argv'|'stdin', buildArgs, modelDiscovery) and the spawn/SSH machinery in src/main/text-generation/commit-message-text-generation.ts. Adding BYO-key providers would mean adding secret storage to an app whose selling point is not needing it. The one transferable idea is `modelCache`'s explicit 7-day TTL + `oco models --refresh`: aio-ade caches discovered models with no visible staleness policy or user-facing refresh.
features.whatItDoes: Normalizes every LLM backend to a single call that takes OpenAI-shaped chat messages and returns a string.

features.howItWorks: `generateCommitMessageFromGitDiff()` in src/commands/commit.ts: a `select` over Yes/No/Edit, `text({ initialValue: commitMessage })` for Edit, and on No a `confirm` that recurses into the same function for a fresh generation. `skipCommitConfirmation` threads the `--yes` flag through. Also handles the zero-staged-files case by offering stage-all or a `multiselect` file picker.
features.name: Regenerate / Edit / confirm loop with --yes escape hatch
features.valueForAioIde: Partial gap. aio-ade writes into an editable commit box (so Edit is free) but regeneration is awkward — SourceControl.tsx:6541 literally tells the user 'Clear the message to regenerate.' A plain Regenerate button that discards and re-runs is a small UI change with real ergonomic payoff, especially since generation is a 60 s-timeout subprocess the user has already waited on once.
features.whatItDoes: After showing the draft, offers Yes / No / Edit; Edit opens the message pre-filled for inline editing, No offers regeneration, and `--yes`/`-y` skips confirmation entirely.

features.howItWorks: src/commands/commit.ts compares `getStagedFiles()` (git diff --name-only --cached --relative, .opencommitignore-filtered) against `getChangedFiles()` (git ls-files --modified plus --others --exclude-standard), then either `confirm`s a stage-all or renders a `multiselect` and calls `gitAdd`.
features.name: Auto-stage assistance when nothing is staged
features.valueForAioIde: aio-ade's Source Control panel already provides full staging UI, so this is redundant. Listed only for completeness.
features.whatItDoes: Rather than erroring out on an empty index, offers to stage everything or presents a checkbox picker of modified/untracked files.

features.howItWorks: `action.yml` (node16, main `out/github-action.cjs`) + src/github-action.ts using @actions/core, @actions/exec, @actions/github and @octokit/webhooks-types to read the push payload, regenerate messages per commit, and force-update the ref.
features.name: GitHub Action mode (rewrite pushed commit messages in CI)
features.valueForAioIde: Out of scope for a desktop IDE, and rewriting pushed history is a posture aio-ade should not adopt. Noted so it is not mistaken for a missing capability.
features.whatItDoes: Runs as a GitHub Action that replaces the messages of freshly pushed commits with AI-generated ones.

integrationRisks: Executing repo code: `@commitlint/load` resolves and runs the target repo's `commitlint.config.js` in-process. aio-ade opens arbitrary cloned repositories, so this is remote-code-execution-by-opening-a-folder inside the Electron main process. Must run in a separate short-lived child process with a timeout, or parse only static config (`.commitlintrc.json`/`.commitlintrc.yml`/package.json `commitlint` key) and refuse `.js`/`.ts` configs. Do not lift it into main as-is.

Worktree/monorepo path resolution: opencommit hardcodes `process.env.PWD` in src/modules/commitlint/constants.ts and calls `load()` with no cwd argument. aio-ade is worktree-per-task with a pnpm workspace, so every path must become an explicit worktree-root parameter. `process.env.PWD` is also unset on Windows, which is aio-ade's primary platform here.

Module-level config reads: prompts.ts, commit.ts and commitlint/prompts.ts all do `const config = getConfig()` at import time. Copying these files verbatim into aio-ade would bind prompt behavior to import order and break per-repo/per-operation overrides, which is the whole point of aio-ade's resolveSourceControlAiForOperation. Every vendored function needs its config passed as an argument.

Prompt-size regression: FULL_GITMOJI_SPEC is ~70 emoji/description lines and the commitlint rule list can be 30+ instructions. aio-ade pipes prompts to CLI agents via stdin/argv with a 200 KB diff budget; a large prefix eats diff budget silently. Whatever is added must be counted against STAGED_DIFF_BYTE_BUDGET, and the argv path already has Windows batch-length constraints (see getSpawnArgsForWindows / UnsafeWindowsBatchArgumentsError).

LLM-generated cached artifacts: the commitlint path asks the model to emit JSON, then salvages it with string surgery (`getJSONBlock`, `removeDoubleNewlines`, replaying prompts out of the response) before `JSON.parse` — which can throw on a bad response. If ported, treat the generated example as optional: fall back to the static example rather than failing generation. Also decide whether the cache file lands in the repo (opencommit writes `.opencommit-commitlint` to the repo root, dirtying the user's tree — aio-ade should keep it in app data).

Two live base prompts already drift in aio-ade: `buildCommitMessagePrompt` (src/shared/commit-message-generation.ts) and `COMMIT_MESSAGE_BASE_PROMPT`/`buildCommitPrompt` (src/shared/commit-message-prompt.ts) encode overlapping but non-identical rules and both are referenced. Consolidate before adding convention toggles, or the toggles will only take effect on one code path.

Diff exclusion is a behavior change with a visible failure mode: excluding lockfiles means a commit that *only* bumps pnpm-lock.yaml yields an empty diff. `getStagedCommitContext` already degrades to the file-name summary when the patch is unreadable — route the all-excluded case through that same fallback rather than returning null.

Hook installation is the highest-blast-radius item: it writes into `.git/hooks`, must honor `core.hooksPath`, collides with husky/lefthook (the common case in the repos aio-ade targets), and needs a self-invocation entry point that an Electron app does not naturally have. Treat as a separate opt-in project, not part of a prompt-quality port.

Attribution/licensing hygiene: MIT permits vendoring but requires the copyright notice to travel. Vendored files need a header crediting Dima Sukharev / opencommit, and the notice should be reflected in aio-ade's third-party licenses.

Test-fixture assumption: opencommit's commitlint e2e fixtures cover commitlint v9, v18 and v19 (test/e2e/prompt-module/data/) because the load API shifted. Any port needs the same matrix or it will break on whichever major the user's repo pins.
license: MIT — `LICENSE` reads "MIT License / Copyright (c) Dima Sukharev, https://github.com/di-sukharev". Fully compatible with vendoring into an MIT Electron app (aio-ade's own LICENSE is MIT, "Copyright (c) 2026 Lovecast Inc."). Attribution in a NOTICE or file header is the only obligation. Note the modules I recommend vendoring pull `@commitlint/types` (MIT) and `@dqbd/tiktoken` (MIT) as transitive deps.
oneLiner: A Node CLI that reads `git diff --staged`, sends it to one of ~14 LLM providers with a heavily-configurable conventional-commit/gitmoji/commitlint-aware prompt, and commits the generated message — optionally wired in as a `prepare-commit-msg` git hook.
reusablePointers: src/modules/commitlint/prompts.ts — the `llmReadableRules` primitives + `rulesPrompts` table + `inferPromptsFromCommitlintConfig()`. Pure functions over @commitlint's QualifiedConfig; the single most valuable artifact in the repo. Strip the module-level `getConfig()`/`i18n` reads and pass options in.

src/modules/commitlint/pwd-commitlint.ts — resolving the *target repo's* @commitlint/load across CJS(<=v18)/ESM(>=v19) and pnpm node_modules layouts. Non-obvious, battle-tested; aio-ade needs exactly this to read a worktree's commitlint config.

src/modules/commitlint/{utils,crypto,constants,types}.ts — hash-keyed cache of derived prompts (sha256 of the config JSON, regenerate only on change). ~80 lines total; maps cleanly onto caching per worktree path.

src/prompts.ts — GITMOJI_HELP (10 pairs) and FULL_GITMOJI_SPEC (~70 pairs) as data, plus `INIT_DIFF_PROMPT` (the canned example diff) and `getConsistencyContent()`'s emoji/omit-scope/one-line-aware example assembly.

verdict:
Vendor selectively — take the prompt layer, ignore everything else. aio-ade's execution layer (CLI-agent spawn, SSH, WSL, model discovery, cancellation, failure sanitization, per-repo/per-operation recipes) is well beyond opencommit's, and opencommit's provider abstraction is actively wrong for an app that intentionally holds no API keys. What aio-ade is thin on is exactly what opencommit is thick on: what goes *into* the prompt.

Concretely, in priority order:
1. Lockfile/binary exclusion in `getStagedCommitContext` (src/main/git/status.ts). ~15 lines, S effort, immediately improves every generation in a pnpm monorepo. Do this first.
2. `<think>` tag stripping into `cleanGeneratedCommitMessage`. ~60 lines, no deps, and aio-ade ships thinking levels up to 'max' so this is a live bug not a hypothetical.
3. Structured convention toggles (conventional-commit / gitmoji-10 / gitmoji-full / omit-scope / one-line / add-WHY / output language) plus a localized few-shot example, replacing the single free-text prompt box. Consolidate the two drifting base prompts while you are in there.
4. Commitlint integration — the genuinely differentiating port, and the only one aio-ade cannot approximate today (grep confirms zero commitlint awareness). Vendor `llmReadableRules`/`rulesPrompts`/`inferPromptsFromCommitlintConfig` as pure functions, but do NOT lift `pwd-commitlint.ts` into the main process unchanged: running a repo's `commitlint.config.js` in-process is RCE-on-folder-open for an IDE that opens arbitrary clones. Sandbox it in a child process or restrict to static config files.

Skip: all 14 provider engines, tiktoken budgeting, the parallel chunk-and-merge generator, the GitHub Action, and the layered ini/.env config system. Defer: the prepare-commit-msg hook (real value for terminal- and agent-driven commits, but husky/lefthook collisions and `core.hooksPath` handling make it its own project).
